en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
4. The Story of the Fourth Throne-Vimāna “Your sublime throne is made of beryl;
swift as thought, it goes wherever you desire.”
Adorned with garlands, wearing fine clothes,
you shine like lightning upon a mountain peak.
By what means do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those enjoyments that are dear to the mind arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
when you were a human being, what merit did you perform?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your complexion shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she gave an answer regarding the fruit of that action:
"This is the fruit of my own small deed."
In this very way, I possessed such blazing power when I was a human being among humans in my previous birth in the world of men.
I saw a stainless monk,
serene and undisturbed;
I gave him a seat.
With my own hands, full of faith.
Because of that, such is my complexion;
because of that, I am successful here.
And wealth arises for me,
whatever is dear to the mind.
I declare this to you, O monk of great power.
"While I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds;
therefore, my power blazes forth in this way,
and my complexion shines in all directions."
The fourth story, the Fourth Seat Mansion, is finished.
